resources.string: Displays a translucent visual band above the on-screen keyboard to reduce typed text visibility to people nearby. Never reads, stores, or transmits typed content.
Enable accessibility access to allow Vanish to follow your keyboard.
Higher opacity reduces visibility more, but dims the keys and text you type.
Portion of the screen above the keyboard covered by the veil.
How far the veil reaches into the keyboard. Set to 0% to leave the keyboard completely clear.
Schematic. Your keyboard layout may differ.
Vanish activates automatically whenever the on-screen keyboard appears, and dismisses when the keyboard closes.
Vanish uses Android’s Accessibility API solely to observe keyboard window bounds. It has no network access and cannot read your typed text.

Vanish is strictly event-driven. It uses no background polling loops, no foreground notification, and zero CPU when the keyboard is closed. Some device manufacturers may still stop background services.
Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET)

Android describes accessibility access as able to observe your actions and retrieve window content. Vanish uses this access strictly to detect when the keyboard window appears and calculate its bounds. Vanish has zero network permissions, stores no logs, and never reads or records your keystrokes, passwords, or screen contents.
Open system Accessibility settings, find Vanish in installed apps or downloaded services, and switch it on.
If the toggle is greyed out on Android 13 or later for sideloaded apps: Open Settings → Apps → Vanish → tap the top-right three dots → select “Allow restricted settings”, then return here.
Waiting for accessibility service to connect…
Tap here to bring up your keyboard
Typed text in this field is not stored or logged.

• Software overlay: reduces visibility from side angles, but does not guarantee privacy against direct view.
• Vanish does not prevent screenshots, screen recording, or observation by other apps.
• Does not work on system-protected screens where Android forbids overlays (e.g. permission dialogs).
• Floating, split, or third-party keyboards that do not report standard window bounds may not trigger the band.
Derive accent colors from system wallpaper (Android 12+).
Restore opacity, coverage, and overlap to default values.
This will restore opacity to 55%, coverage to 100%, and keyboard overlap to 0%.
